title: Seeing Others: How Recognition Works and How it Can Help Heal a Divided World
speaker_position: Professor of Sociology and African and African American Studies and Robert I. Goldman Professor of European Studies
abstract: Michèle Lamont examines how boundaries between different groups have been made more rigid due to cultural processes, and how breaking down these boundaries must move beyond simple calls for empathy. Instead, Dr. Lamont notes that we can examine the cultural structures and repertoires that create these boundaries and transform these narratives to be more fluid and inclusive.

title: The APS and the Pursuit of Happiness
abstract: Jeffrey Rosen talks about what the notion of "the pursuit of happiness" meant for Thomas Jefferson and Ben Franklin, who understood that happiness in pursuit is an active process, rather than a feeling. In this light, happiness is found virtue, self-improvement, and lifelong learning. Dr. Rosen further explores how the Founding Fathers applied this notion to their own pursuits, including Ben Franklin's founding of the American Philosophical Society as an offshoot of the Junto, Franklin's club designed to inspire virtuous learning.
proceedings_title: The APS and the Pursuit of Happiness

title: Individual Specialization in a Generalist Apex Predator: The Leopard Seal
abstract: Emily S. Sperou discusses her research leopard seals, focusing on insights into their foraging strategies and reproductive behaviors. Dr. Sperou's research also highlights the importance of studying individual behaviors in apex predators like leopard seals in order to understand their role in shaping ecosystems.
proceedings_title: Individual Specialization in a Generalist Apex Predator: The Leopard Seal

title: Postcolonial Provenance Research, Transcultural Cooperation and Restitution Practices: Lessons Learnt from the Humboldt Forum
abstract: Hermann Parzinger examines the development of the Humboldt Forum, a cultural center built in Berlin, Germany, and the colonial history through which cultural objects were collected. Like many museums in colonial countries, these items were obtained through looting. Drawing from his work with the Humboldt Forum, Dr. Parzinger details the need for museums to recognize their colonial histories, to understand the provenance of objects and work toward restitution, and to develop transcultural relationships.
proceedings_title: Postcolonial Provenance Research, Transcultural Cooperation, and Restitution Practices: Lessons Learnt from the Humboldt Forum

speaker_position: James S. McDonnell Distinguished University Professor
abstract: Eddie Glaude, Jr. reflects on the power of ordinary people to achieve change and justice, a power that has otherwise been left to politicians and the ruling classes. title: From 'Chasing My Cure' to 'Every Cure': Unlocking Solutions Hiding in Plain Sight
abstract: David Fajgenbaum discusses getting diagnosed with and nearly dying five times from Castleman's Disease while in medical school at the University of Pennsylvania. After the fourth relapse, Dr. Fajgenbaum realized he needed a treatment for himself that repurposed an already existing drug. Dr. Fajgenbaum discusses establishing the Castle Disease Collaborative Network (CDCN) and began researching, before eventually discovering a drug that has successfully kept him in remission for 11 years and has helped others. Further, Dr. Fajgenbaum details his research into repurposing drug treatments for diseases they were not created for.
proceedings_title: From Chasing My Cure to Every Cure: Unlocking Solutions Hiding in Plain Sight
